title: TreeSet — sorting custom objects, Comparable vs Comparator, Red-Black tree
shortTitle: How does TreeSet sort custom objects?

s1_definition.profdef: `TreeSet` keeps its elements sorted using a Red-Black tree, a self-balancing binary search tree, so add, remove and contains are all O(log n). To sort custom objects the element class must either implement `Comparable<T>` to define a natural ordering through `compareTo`, or you must pass a `Comparator<T>` to the TreeSet constructor. Without either, TreeSet throws `ClassCastException` on the first add.
s1_definition.analogy: TreeSet is a filing cabinet that automatically keeps accounts in sorted order the moment you drop them in. The cabinet needs to know the sorting rule: either each account card knows how to compare itself (Comparable), or the bank manager hands the cabinet a sorting rule book (Comparator).
s1_definition.oneliner: TreeSet is a Red-Black tree giving sorted O(log n) order; elements need Comparable or a Comparator or you get ClassCastException.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** `TreeSet` keeps its elements sorted using a Red-Black tree, a self-balancing binary search tree, so add, remove and contains are all O(log n). To sort custom objects the element class must either implement `Comparable<T>` to define a natural ordering through `compareTo`, or you must pass a `Comparator<T>` to the TreeSet constructor. Without either, TreeSet throws `ClassCastException` on the first add.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** TreeSet is a filing cabinet that automatically keeps accounts in sorted order the moment you drop them in. The cabinet needs to know the sorting rule: either each account card knows how to compare itself (Comparable), or the bank manager hands the cabinet a sorting rule book (Comparator).

**One line to remember:** TreeSet is a Red-Black tree giving sorted O(log n) order; elements need Comparable or a Comparator or you get ClassCastException.

sections.s3_banking: At the National Bank of India this came up directly when handling sorting custom objects in a TreeSet. Rajesh holds savings account SAV2001 with a balance of 1,000,000 rupees and Priya holds current account CUR3001 with 250,000 rupees, and the team needed the collection behaviour to be exactly correct so balances and account lists were never wrong. The runnable demo below reproduces the situation and proves the behaviour with a small test.

sections.s6_takeaway:
TreeSet maintains a fully sorted set using a self-balancing Red-Black tree, giving guaranteed O(log n) operations. Custom objects must either implement Comparable for a natural ordering or be supplied with a Comparator at construction time.

In the National Bank portfolio service I used a TreeSet with a Comparator on balance to keep accounts like Rajesh's SAV2001 and Priya's CUR3001 permanently sorted for leaderboard reports. I always remembered that TreeSet decides equality through the comparator, so I made sure my comparator reflected the true business notion of a duplicate to avoid silently dropping accounts with identical balances.

In an interview I would stress that I always use BigDecimal for money, keep map keys immutable, and pick the collection whose ordering and complexity match the banking access pattern, because in a system that moves real money, choosing the wrong data structure is not a style issue, it is a correctness and reliability issue.

keyPoints: Objects must implement Comparable (natural order) or provide Comparator
Comparable: class defines its own ordering via compareTo()
Comparator: external ordering — passed to TreeSet constructor
Red-Black tree maintains sorted order after every insertion
